key_insight: Spin-polarized DFT predicts that pressure tunes EuCd2As2’s mechanical and thermophysical properties while preserving mechanical stability from 0 to 8 GPa.
engineering_relevance: Its predicted magnetic moment and strong visible–ultraviolet absorption suggest potential for spintronic and optoelectronic materials engineering.
method: Structural, elastic, acoustic, and thermophysical calculations.
Ferromagnetic band structure, DOS, magnetic, and optical analysis.
evidence_signal: Zero-pressure lattice parameters agree with experiment; calculations predict a pressure-induced brittle-to-ductile transition, no Fermi-level band gap at 0 GPa, and a net moment of 6.96 μB per unit cell.
watch_item: Pressure-dependent predictions and device relevance require experimental validation; the reported electronic pressure study considers the ferromagnetic phase.
paper_title: Pressure dependent DFT study of mechanical, thermal, electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of EuCd2As2: a magnetic semimetal
